parallel.requirements: The run recognized the std-only Rust 2021 migration, Cargo-compatible project, /output/test19.rs entry, byte-for-byte output, black-box executable probing, and ignored CLI argument behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although swarm mode was active, the main agent declared the task single and self-contained, declined subagents, and kept exploration, implementation, integration, verification, and final response under one owner.
parallel.implementation: It captured the reference bytes, inferred the spinner sequence, progress display, and formatting behavior, then wrote Cargo.toml, test19.rs, and modules under /output/indicators.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: It delivered a package with a root binary source, an indicators module tree, Cargo metadata, and built executables recorded by artifact validation.
parallel.verification: It compiled with rustc, compared Rust and C++ outputs through xxd/diff, built with Cargo release, and compared the Cargo binary output for an argument case.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or evaluator-visible incorrect behavior remained; the official status evaluation passed all 40 testcases.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same std-only Rust 2021 migration, byte-for-byte output requirement, Cargo structure, black-box probing requirement, and command-line argument behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single main agent owned all work directly, with no delegation, no child handoffs, and no split ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: It probed reference output and argument behavior, inferred the Braille spinner and formatting, collected std::env::args(), then wrote Cargo.toml, test19.rs, and src library modules.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It delivered a Cargo package with src/lib.rs, component modules, root test19.rs, /output/test19, and target/release/test19.
serial.verification: It built the Cargo release binary, built the standalone rustc binary, compared both outputs against the C++ executable with arbitrary arguments, ran cargo test --release, and cleaned temporary output files.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or evaluator-visible incorrect behavior remained; the official status evaluation passed all 40 testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel attempt saw the same source program and requirements, including Rust 2021, std-only implementation, byte-identical output, root test19.rs, and black-box probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt saw the identical source program and requirements and explicitly implemented argument collection while preserving ignored-argument behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both covered the evaluator-relevant requirements; the serial code more literally satisfied the std::env::args() wording, while the parallel code tested ignored arguments and still passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run entered swarm mode, then the main agent stated that subagents would add coordination cost and performed the migration directly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had one main agent and no delegation, so all implementation, build, and verification ownership stayed local.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no multi-agent ownership split in either trajectory; parallel differed only by having a swarm-mode preamble and an explicit no-delegation decision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: With no children, there were no child briefs, cross-agent contracts, or returned handoffs; the main agent selected a simple indicators module API internally.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run likewise had no cross-agent interface, using local src modules and a root binary that imported them through path attributes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The interface difference was local project layout only: parallel used an indicators/ module directory, while serial used src/ modules plus re-exports.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel main agent inferred the output bytes and wrote CyclicProgress, ProgressDisplay, Format, and the root main program under /output/indicators and test19.rs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main agent inferred the same behavior, wrote analogous components under /output/src, and included an explicit std::env::args().collect() call in test19.rs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementations produced passing behavior; they differed in module layout and API naming for percentage precision, not in official-output behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no delegated child results to join; the main agent observed its own write results, build results, comparison results, and then finalized.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no delegated child results to join; the main agent observed its own write, build, test, cleanup, and final response results.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both result lifecycles were single-threaded and complete, so there was no missing join, trapped verifier result, or unused child result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel main agent wrote all final files itself: Cargo.toml, test19.rs, and indicators module files, with no competing live writer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main agent wrote all final files itself: Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, three src modules, and test19.rs, with no competing live writer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state or merge conflict occurred; the only difference was final project layout and artifact file list.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel attempt compiled with rustc, compared output against the C++ executable byte-for-byte, built Cargo release, checked the Cargo binary with an argument case, and passed the official evaluator.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt built Cargo release, compiled with rustc, compared both outputs against the C++ executable with arbitrary arguments, ran cargo test --release, and passed the official evaluator.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial ran cargo test in addition to output comparisons; both had sufficient acceptance evidence and both officially passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run completed without timeout after 122.266 agent seconds and had no subagent fan-out or delegated budget pressure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run completed without timeout after 168.207 agent seconds and had no subagent fan-out or delegated budget pressure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both closed cleanly; the parallel run was shorter but that was ordinary single-agent execution, not parallel coordination.

outcome_analysis.explanation: This is a both_pass pair. The current completed official evaluations in cell/status.json show both modes passed 40 of 40 testcases. The parallel run did not actually execute a child-agent or multi-agent mechanism; it only had swarm mode enabled and then solved the task directly. The serial run followed a similar direct single-agent path with slightly broader local verification.
parallel_contributors: No adverse parallel-side contributor is evidenced because no child or multi-agent mechanism executed.
serial_contributors: The serial attempt independently implemented and verified the same required behavior with a direct single-agent workflow.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel organized modules under indicators/ while serial organized them under src/.
Serial explicitly collected std::env::args(), while parallel treated arguments as ignored after testing an argument case.
